figure1_chain_budget: Recovery, reagent recycle, purge and qualified cement form one coupled circuit. The paired bars share the same conventional plant inventory. At 30 g/kWh and reagent multiplier 1.30, conventional emissions are 756.9 and selected basalt emissions 636.0 kg per tonne: 456 kg avoided carbonate emissions pay for 335.1 kg added recovery emissions, leaving 120.9 kg net savings.
figure2_survival_region: A contour plot shows 10 and 20 percent reduction boundaries narrowing as reagent demand or electricity intensity rises. The selected multiplier 1.30 gives 10 percent only below 47.4 g/kWh and 20 percent below 18.3 g/kWh. A second plot shows recovery/selectivity and heat/water penalties separately and combined; the combination can erase the development target. Lines and text duplicate color meaning.
figureS1_burdens: Patterned stacked bars separate recovery electricity, heat, paired makeup, other operations, feed carbonates and fixed burdens. The main target at 30 g/kWh stays below 456 kg avoided emissions; combined penalties and broad extraction consume or exceed the available margin. Percentage labels use paired conventional inventories.
figureS2_partial_replacement: Four distinct line styles show increasing percentage reduction with more calcium replacement at 20, 30, 40 and 50 g/kWh. A fixed active-process charge causes an initial penalty. Full replacement reaches 19.4, 16.0, 12.5 and 9.1 percent respectively; shading marks the 10 to 20 percent development target.
